title: Teacher Dave Perkins and his versatility
summary: Dave Perkins knew Clark's father and taught and played all instruments. The interviewers ask whether he also played drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Who was your teacher, Brother Ray? When did you start up?
Oh, Dave Perkins. He's dead, he's been dead now I guess, oh twenty, oh I guess thirty some odd years. Because he died before my mother did.
Did you ever happen to know who he played with, some of the bands he played with? Well no I didn't.

But he used to talk, he used to tell me all the time about my father. He said I knew Aaron well and he was a good baritone player, a wonderful baritone player. He says, and I used to play trombone with him sometime in the Pickwood band. But you see he was mostly, Dave was mostly an orchestra man. He was mostly an orchestra man. In fact he played all the instruments. Bass, trombone, baritone, trumpet, he taught all the instruments and he played all of them. Clarinets, saxophones, axillophones, he taught all the instruments and he played every one of them.
Did you ever see him play drums in any band?
No, I never seen him play any drums. But I've seen him play all the wind instruments. I've seen him play all the wind instruments. I saw him play all the wind instruments.
I saw a picture of him as a drummer one place.
Well he taught Francis to money a drums. You know Francis? I don't think so. He's a friend of Raymond.
He said he was in Papalina, I thought he was playing drums in that band. Well we'll ask Francis. How long did you take lessons?
